name: Upper Cumberland

counties: Cumberland, Fentress, Macon, Overton, Putnam, Smith, Warren, and White Counties

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Sangiovese, Grenache, Carignan and Zinfandel fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
